articles.abstract: Mainstream historiography of the Indian nationalist and revolutionary movements has predominantly documented elite political trajectories, frequently rendering the massive participation of grassroots women invisible. While women have historically fought against systemic patriarchy and colonial oppression to claim political rights—such as franchise and equal agency—their physical and biological realities within public and revolutionary spaces remain unaddressed. This paper examines the unheralded participation of women in the nationalist and revolutionary movements of Andhra Pradesh, bridging the gap between macro-political resistance and the everyday micro-politics of the female body. Drawing upon primary oral history testimonies of veteran freedom fighters and revolutionary leaders (such as Mallu Swarajyam, Choudary Sampurnamma, Bhoopathi Varalakshmi, and Bidika Mahalakshmamma), this study highlights the 'invisible logistics' of resistance—specifically, sanitation, public washroom accessibility, and menstrual management during guerrilla warfare and mass mobilizations. It argues that true political equality cannot be conceptualized without acknowledging and addressing the biological and structural barriers faced by women in public domains, and explores the paradox of post-independence political marginalization alongside the enduring socio-cultural legacy of these grassroots women.
articles.title: Beyond the Heroic Narrative: Everyday Micro-Politics, Body Politics, and the Gendered Logistics of Resistance in the Nationalist and Revolutionary Movements of Andhra Pradesh

articles.abstract: India's greatest contribution to humanity is not technology or empire, but the science of inner transformation. The entire Indian tradition begins with one critical foundational question: "Who am I?" (Ko'ham?). The movement from "Self to Cosmos", "From inward to outward", and "Atma bodha to Viswa bodha" defines the central trajectory of Indian philosophy. This trajectory is not an escape from the world, but an organic expansion of the individual self until the structural boundary between "I" and "Universe" completely dissolves. The Upaniṣads define this existential state as "Tat Tvam Asi" ("That Thou Art"). Sri Aurobindo maps this as "The Evolution of Consciousness," while the Bhagavad Gῑta frames it as "Yoga" or divine Union. Ultimately, this realization culminates in the global ideal of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam—the absolute recognition that the whole world is one single family.
articles.title: Global Harmony through Consciousness: From Self to Cosmos — An Advaitic Perspective on Universal Unity and Social Action

articles.abstract: In India, the history of microfinance dates back to establishment of Syndicate Bank in 1921 in private sector. During the early years, Syndicate Bank concentrated on raising micro deposits in the form of daily/weekly basis and sanctioned micro loans to its clients for shorter period of time. But microfinance came to limelight only when Dr Yunus gave it a mass movement in Grameen Bank experiment. Microfinance can be called a novel approach to provide saving and investment facility to the poor around world. Improved access and efficient provision of savings, credit, and insurance facilities in particular can enable the poor to smoothen their consumption, manage their risks better, gradually build their asset base, develop their business, enhance their income earning capacity, and enjoy an improved quality of life. In India, microfinance mainly operates through Self Help Group (SHGs), Non Government Organizations(NGOs), and Credit Agencies. It provides poor people with the means to find their own way out of poverty. It put the power squarely in their hands, giving them a larger stake in their own success than one –time donation of food, goods, or cash. The initiatives of Government for poverty alleviation could not succeed to the desired level, may be due to the fact that they do not take cognizance of power of the poor to deal with their own problems. Women who form half of the population and constitute substantial productive and economic resources in our country have been the silent sufferers of this inadequate attention. Overwhelming prove is available to emphasize these rural development strategies that fail to take note of the potential of the women and to make provision of such potentiality to be utilized will not have higher rate of sustainability. It is said that women are also more efficient converters of the resources into income creation, productive purpose and household development. The SHGs have the potential to empower women through socio- economic changes material gain secured through excel to credit and better bargaining power and social changes brought about through group dynamics on sustainable basis. This paper mainly analyses the role of women in rural poverty reduction and how the participation of women in sociological and economical point of view. For the purpose of research around 82 samples were collected randomly from the respondents.
articles.title: Role of Microfinance and Role of Women in Poverty Reduction through Self-Help Groups in Guntur District of Andhra Pradesh

articles.abstract: India's environmental governance rests on an unusual combination: an expansive constitutional commitment to a healthy environment, a dense statutory framework, and a judiciary that has at times acted as the principal environmental regulator. Yet air, water and land indicators remain among the world's poorest, and enforcement outcomes lag far behind legislative ambition. This paper argues that the gap between law and outcome is best explained by weak political accountability and under-resourced, captured or discretion-heavy regulatory institutions, and that recent reforms privilege speed of clearance over answerability. Using a doctrinal and analytical method, it examines the constitutional foundations, the institutional design of regulators and the National Green Tribunal (NGT), the role of the Supreme Court, and the tension between development and ecological limits. It concludes with reforms aimed at statutory independence of regulators, transparent and participatory decision-making, credible penalties, and a constitutionally grounded duty of climate-aware, rights-based development.

articles.abstract:
Traditional artisans constitute an indispensable component of India's cultural economy, preserving centuries old craft traditions while contributing significantly to employment generation, rural livelihoods and sustainable development. Andhra Pradesh (AP), known for its rich heritage of handloom and handicraft products such as Uppada and Venkatagiri sarees, Dharmavaram silk, Kondapalli toys, Etikoppaka lacquerware, Kalamkari textiles and Narsapur lace, presents a compelling case for examining the role of digital transformation in artisan empowerment. The rapid expansion of digital technologies, including e-commerce platforms, digital payment systems, social media and mobile applications, has fundamentally altered how artisans access markets, interact with consumers and establish entrepreneurial identities. Simultaneously, national initiatives such as Digital India, the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC), Government e-Marketplace (GeM) and specialized artisan focused platforms have created new opportunities for inclusive economic participation.

This paper combines contemporary literature, government reports and policy initiatives to evaluate how digital inclusion and technology influence market access for traditional workers and artisans in AP. It argues that digital platforms have evolved beyond commercial marketplaces to become instruments of entrepreneurship, financial inclusion, cultural preservation and livelihood diversification. However, the paper also highlights persistent barriers including digital literacy gaps, infrastructural disparities, branding limitations, logistical challenges and unequal access to digital resources that continue to restrict the equitable benefits of digital transformation. The study concludes that sustainable empowerment requires an integrated ecosystem where technological innovation is complemented by institutional support, capacity building, digital skills and collaborative governance. Strengthening such an ecosystem will not only improve artisans' economic resilience but also contribute to preserving AP's unique cultural heritage in an increasingly digital economy.

articles.title: Technology, Digital Inclusion and Market Access: Evaluating the Role of Digital Platforms and E-Commerce in Empowering Traditional Workers and Artisans of Andhra Pradesh

articles.abstract: Voting behaviour is an essential component of democratic politics and provides an important basis for understanding the functioning of representative democracy. It reflects the political preferences, attitudes, perceptions and motivations of citizens in choosing their representatives and evaluating the policies and programmes of political parties. The study of voting behaviour extends beyond electoral statistics and voting patterns to examine the social, economic, psychological and political factors influencing electoral choices. In the Indian political system, caste continues to be one of the significant determinants of voting behaviour, despite constitutional provisions promoting equality, social justice and the prohibition of caste-based discrimination. The deep-rooted nature of the caste system and its influence on social relationships have contributed to the growing interaction between caste and politics. Political parties frequently consider caste composition while selecting candidates, formulating electoral strategies, mobilizing voters and consolidating political support. The politicization of caste and the caste-based mobilization of political communities have consequently become important features of electoral politics in India. Caste associations, community identities and regional political formations have also influenced electoral competition and political representation. However, caste does not operate independently; it interacts with other factors such as economic interests, political leadership, development, ideology, religion and regional aspirations. The present article examines the relationship between caste and voting behaviour in India, with particular emphasis on the politicization of caste, caste-based electoral mobilization and the strategies adopted by political parties. It argues that understanding the influence of caste is essential for analyzing electoral dynamics, democratic representation and the changing nature of Indian politics.
articles.title: Voting Behaviour in India with Special Emphasis on Caste in Indian Political System
